transcript: I saw every show in the 2023-2024 Broadway season finishing it off with Mary Jane starring Rachel McAdams. Mary Jane is a single mother caring for a two year old son who is seriously ill and whose life is more or less always on the line. In this play, we see Mary Jane in a series of scenes and interactions with various women in her life who, each in their own way, help her navigate or make sense of her situation. Based on the subject matter, it's obviously a heavy show but it wasn't as explosively cathartic as I thought it would be, which I actually thought was a big strength of this play. It didn't really need to go there as the premise is inherently emotional enough and the characters and conversational writing is very captivating. Rachel McAdams is amazing in the titular role. The selflessness Mary Jane brings to the way she cares for her child is similar to the selflessness Rachel McAdams brings to caring for the text —there's no time or space for frills and personal indulgences, the priority really is to provide. With this, Rachel McAdams exemplifies so much restraint and depth and precision in her performance. It's not an easy feat to embody a character who, in some ways, exists only in service of someone else but is still fully developed. Needless to say, I feel like her Tony nom is very well deserved. Mary Jane is running on Broadway through June 30th. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer clearly attended and appreciated the show, praising Rachel McAdams' performance as 'amazing' and calling her Tony nomination 'very well deserved.' While noting it wasn't as cathartic as expected, they frame this as 'a big strength' and describe the writing as 'captivating.'
